description: Cuts a window of a Twitch or Kick stream (a VOD, or a live stream so far) into a finished 1080x1920 MP4 and returns a download link, without opening the web editor. Follows find_clip_moments: the same source and a moment's t_start_s and t_end_s (5 to 60 seconds). Layouts: fit (full frame over a blurred fill, the safe default), split (facecam on top, gameplay below; facecam names the corner it is in), crop (centre crop). Optional hook text is burned in at the top. Captions of the streamer's speech are burned in by default, in the editor's Bold look at the bottom: the speech is read on the heistclips server with open-source Whisper (English, German, French, Portuguese, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Turkish; the language is detected), and no outside AI service sees the clip. captions false leaves them off; caption_look and caption_position change their style. A clip that comes back without captions (no speech, another language, the day's server limit, or a slow read) still comes back, with captions_reason saying why and an add_captions link that opens it in the editor, where the speech is read on the person's own device. Each cut uses one clip credit, the same as a render on the site: a new account gets free clips, then packs. The first call returns an account code; passed back as account on later cut_clip and post_clip calls, it carries credits and connected YouTube/TikTok accounts over. Usually done in 10 to 40 seconds. It never hangs: if the file is not ready after about 45 seconds the result has status 'cutting' and a job code instead of a download link. cut_clip_status with that job waits for the file, while a second cut_clip for the same window would start a second job. Nothing is charged until the file exists. The file is kept 72 hours. A second version of a clip that is not a copy (so a platform's repost check and a campaign's duplicate rule see a different file): pass variant 2, 3 or 4 with the same source, start and end. Each variant is a fixed, different render of the same moment: 1 = the moment as picked, the chosen caption look and position, hook at the top (the default, today's render); 2 = starts 1.5 s earlier and ends 1.5 s later, the next caption look, captions on the other edge (bottom becomes top), hook in the lower third; 3 = starts 1 s later and ends 1 s earlier, the look after that, captions where they were, hook at the top; 4 = shifted 1 s later and 1.5 s longer, a fourth look, captions on the other edge, hook in the lower third. Windows stay inside 5 to 60 seconds. Pass the first cut's clip_id as variant_of so the result names it. Every variant uses one clip credit like any cut (pricing is per clip); the result's next_variant says which version to ask for next.

account.description: The account code (hc_…) from an earlier cut_clip. Leave out on the very first cut.

caption_look.description: Caption style: bold = big white uppercase (default); karaoke = word by word, the spoken word in yellow; green = word by word, the spoken word in green and the rest white; clean = plain white sentence case; neon = the whole line lime green with a glow; boxed = dark text on a white box

captions.description: Burn in captions of the streamer's speech (default true). false = no captions.

end.description: Where the clip ends: seconds into the stream (t_end_s), or h:mm:ss. 5 to 60 seconds after start.

facecam.description: For split: the corner of the stream the facecam is in (default tr = top right)

hook.description: Optional text burned in at the top, e.g. one of the moment's hooks. Up to 90 characters; emoji are dropped.

layout.description: fit = whole frame, blurred fill (default); split = facecam on top + gameplay; crop = centre crop

source.description: The stream: a Twitch VOD link or id, a Kick video link, or a channel (its live or latest stream). Use the stream url from find_clip_moments.

start.description: Where the clip starts: seconds into the stream (t_start_s), or h:mm:ss

variant.description: Which version of this moment to render (default 1, today's render). 2, 3 and 4 are each a different trim, caption look, caption position and hook placement of the same moment, so the file is not a copy of version 1. Uses one clip credit like any cut.

variant_of.description: The clip_id of the first cut this is a version of; echoed back in the result.

name: cut_clip
title: Cut a moment into a vertical 9:16 MP4 clip for TikTok, Shorts and Reels
